verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: new Section 12.1.3 supplies the SFJ IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions (PB modifications, combinations with non-SFJ items, PB specifications), the procure/modify/replace ladder, the refund backstop, and a 3× annual-amounts super-cap scoped only to 12.1.3 so SFJ's existing uncapped indemnities are untouched. Preferred is not complete: no express duty to defend, no breach-of-applicable-law or data-breach limbs, PB's indemnity at 12.1.2 remains far broader than Customer content plus breach of law, and control-of-defence/cooperation mechanics are not in the rendered text (cannot be verified). Minimality holds. The narrowing of 12.1.2(f) from "either Party" to "PB" is not gratuitous: left unchanged it would require PB to indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance, directly circling back on and neutralising the new 12.1.3, and the rule's own redline guidance contemplates narrowing Customer's indemnity where the clause is one-sided. The 12.2.1 cross-reference edit is a necessary conforming change so notice mechanics reach 12.1.3. The cap floor ("in no event less than three times the aggregate amounts payable by PB to SFJ ... in the first twelve (12) months in which such amounts become due") does not exceed the 3×-annual threshold in substance — it is the same multiple applied to a different annual period — and is necessary because PB's payments to SFJ are Approval-triggered, so a pure trailing-twelve-month cap would be zero (and the indemnity worthless) for most of the term. Intent preserved: the loss/net-of-tax-benefit mechanics, the mutual gross-negligence/material-breach carve-outs in 12.1.1 and 12.1.2, and the notice regime survive without contradiction; no defined term is orphaned and the only cross-reference touched is conformed. Drafting point to tighten (not a completeness failure): the refund is measured by "the amounts paid by PB to SFJ for the affected item", but PB's payments under this Agreement are Approval Payments rather than item-priced consideration. Consider "a pro-rata portion of the amounts paid by PB to SFJ attributable to the affected item, or if not separately attributable, the amounts paid in the preceding twelve (12) months" to avoid an indeterminate refund base. If pushing for the preferred position, add (i) "defend" plus SFJ control of the defence to 12.1.1/12.1.3, (ii) limbs for SFJ's breach of applicable law and unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ, and (iii) a narrowing of 12.1.2 to PB-provided content and PB's breach of law.
